title: Copilot Studio: credit costs per agent and by lifecycle stage in the Monitor tab
summary: Hold: the allocation API operation exists, but the printed call omits the environment scope and the request structure and values needed to use it. The roadmap facts and the documented monitoring and spending-control behavior are supported; the maker navigation also needs its supporting source cited.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans per-agent consumption cost visibility for makers in Copilot Studio's Monitor tab.
claims.quote: Now makers will have clear visibility into their consumption costs directly within Monitor tab at both a per-agent level and an estimated breakdown of those costs across the agents lifecylce.

claims.claim: The planned estimated lifecycle breakdown includes activities such as authoring, testing, evaluations and production usage.
claims.quote: This will allow makers to see costs distributed across activities such as authoring, testing, evaluations, and production usage, helping connect overall consumption to specific actions and experiences.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Preview credit figures are near-real-time estimates.
claims.quote: The estimates in Preview and Evaluate are near-real-time approximations that give you immediate visibility into how many credits an action is likely to consume, without waiting for the full billing pipeline to complete.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Evaluate credit figures are near-real-time estimates.
claims.quote: The estimates in Preview and Evaluate are near-real-time approximations that give you immediate visibility into how many credits an action is likely to consume, without waiting for the full billing pipeline to complete.

claims.claim: Monitor's credit view updates a few times a day.
claims.quote: The view in Monitor is updated a few times a day and shows the accurate number of credits consumed for all events processed up to that point.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Monitor reflects processed events and is the authoritative credit figure used for billing, subject to processing delay.
claims.quote: Unlike the near-real-time estimates you see in Preview and Evaluate, the value shown in Monitor reflects all events processed up to that point and is the final, source-of-truth number used for billing.

claims.claim: Final credit consumption appears in Monitor within a few hours of the estimated activity.
claims.quote: Those events are then processed, and the final, accurate number is reflected in Monitor within a few hours.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs rather than its individual maker or users.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged to the environment where the agent runs, from prepaid capacity or through the environment's pay-as-you-go billing plan, and not to the individual makers or users who run agents.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rationale: cost

claims.claim: For the Microsoft Copilot harness, billing begins during building rather than only after publication.
claims.quote: Unlike the standard harness, which starts billing after publish, the Microsoft Copilot harness charges credits from the moment you start building.

claims.claim: Previewing Microsoft Copilot harness agents can consume credits before publication.
claims.quote: Agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness consume Copilot Credits while makers build, preview, and evaluate them, before those agents enter a formal production lifecycle.

claims.claim: Evaluating Microsoft Copilot harness agents can consume credits before publication.
claims.quote: Agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness consume Copilot Credits while makers build, preview, and evaluate them, before those agents enter a formal production lifecycle.

claims.claim: An exploration environment can incur consumption even when its Microsoft Copilot harness agents are never published.
claims.quote: An environment used for maker exploration can incur consumption even if its agents are never published for production use.

claims.claim: Standard-harness Monitor reports billed credits only.
claims.quote: The agent's Monitor page in Copilot Studio shows the agent's billed credits over time. It shows billed credits only, so it can show less consumption than these reports, which also include non-billed credits.

claims.quote:
On the navigation pane, select Licensing.

On the Summary tab, select Manage Agents.

claims.where: controls[0].api; controls[0].note; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: No API operation for setting an individual agent's monthly credit limit was found, and the governance article names none.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio agent monthly credit limit API set Stop usage automated; "Copilot Studio" "agent" "monthly limit" "API" "licensing". Read govern-credit-consumption, manage-usage-microsoft-copilot-harness and the allocations tutorial; no agent-limit operation found.

claims.claim: Administrators can set monthly credit consumption limits per Copilot Studio agent in prepaid or pay-as-you-go environments.
claims.quote: Admins can set monthly consumption limits for each Copilot Studio agent, regardless of whether the environment uses prepaid capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Governance controls: first table row
claims.claim: Agent limit notifications alert environment and tenant administrators as usage approaches the configured limit.
claims.quote: Notifications: Admins, both at the environment and tenant level, receive alerts when an agent's usage approaches the defined limit.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: An agent monthly limit can turn off the agent when Stop usage is enabled.
claims.quote: Turn on Stop usage if the agent should be turned off when it reaches the limit.

claims.claim: Agent limits are not applied instantly.
claims.quote: Limits aren't applied instantly. An agent can continue to respond for some time after it reaches its limit, so set limits and notification thresholds with some margin.

claims.claim: Learn recommends using a recurring or automated process to apply an organization's standard development limit to individual agents.
claims.quote: If your organization defines a standard limit for new agents, use a recurring or automated process to apply it to individual agents.

In the Licensing pane, under Products, select Copilot Studio.
Select the Summary tab.
[...] Under the Copilot Studio heading, select Manage Copilot Credits or Manage sessions.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: The printed PUT allocationsV2 line with prose about entitlementId, quantity and a TenantPool rule is a usable allocation call once placeholders are filled.
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].api.call and the matching rendered call with: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01; Authorization: Bearer <access-token>; Content-Type: application/json; body {"scope":{"environmentId":"<environment-id>"},"allocatedEntitlements":[{"entitlementId":"MCSMessages","allocation":{"quantity":<quantity>},"enforcementRules":[{"ruleType":"TenantPool","enabled":<true-or-false>}]}]}. The endpoint and version are documented through variables in the cited tutorial; the pre-check's literal-string miss is not evidence that the endpoint is absent.

claims.where: controls[1].governs, scope; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: The environment allocation controls assigned credits and whether the environment can draw unallocated tenant capacity.
claims.quote: In the allocation panel, select an environment and specify the number of Copilot Credits to allocate in the Copilot Credits textbox. [...] Select Draw from the available capacity in my tenant to let the environment use unallocated prepaid capacity from the tenant pool.

claims.claim: Managing Copilot Studio capacity requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent role able to manage licensing and capacity.
claims.quote: To manage Copilot Studio capacity, you need the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls: second table row
claims.claim: Environment capacity controls apply to all Copilot Studio workloads in the environment.
claims.quote: Environment capacity controls apply to all Copilot Studio workloads in the environment, not only agents powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: An agent's monthly credit limit does not stop agent flows it calls.
claims.quote: An agent's monthly limit doesn't stop the agent flows that the agent calls. Agent flows are billed and checked for capacity separately, and new agent flow runs are blocked only when the environment has no Copilot Credits available.

claims.claim: Agent limits do not cap aggregate environment consumption.
claims.quote: Agent limits don't cap aggregate environment consumption.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center does not provide a tenant-wide default agent limit.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin center doesn't provide a tenant-wide default agent limit.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Containing prepaid environment consumption requires a defined allocation with tenant-capacity draw turned off.
claims.quote: To contain prepaid consumption, allocate a defined amount of Copilot Credits to the environment and turn off Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Cost and licensing; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling tenant-capacity draw does not prevent continued consumption through a linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: When you clear this option, the environment doesn't draw from unallocated prepaid capacity in the tenant after it consumes its allocation. If the environment is linked to a pay-as-you-go billing plan, usage can continue through the linked Azure subscription.

claims.claim: Learn points to Power Platform API entitlement insight operations for retrieving consumption data programmatically.
claims.quote: At scale or when using automation, use the entitlement insight operations in the Power Platform API to retrieve consumption data programmatically.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio environment and agent spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center are opt-in.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio environment and agent policies are opt-in; existing Power Platform admin center controls continue to apply until a Microsoft 365 spending policy covers that scope.

claims.claim: Existing Power Platform admin center spending controls apply until a Microsoft 365 spending policy covers the relevant scope.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio environment and agent policies are opt-in; existing Power Platform admin center controls continue to apply until a Microsoft 365 spending policy covers that scope.

claims.claim: Learn suggests classifying environments as exploration, test and validation, or funded production.
claims.quote: Classify environments as exploration, test and validation, or funded production. Define the approved capacity posture and exception process for each classification.
